text: 者ども、道を開け!
translation: Everyone, make way!

vocabulary.meaning: you all, you people (rough/commanding address to a group)

grammar: 道を開け is a command form (imperative) of 道を開ける. 者ども is an archaic/rough plural address used by those in authority. The sentence has the forceful register of a military or ceremonial order.

text: 召喚し言うなよ。
translation: Don't tell me to summon.

vocabulary.meaning: don't (do something) — casual negative command with mild admonishment

grammar: 〜するなよ is a casual negative imperative. The particle よ adds a tone of exasperation or insistence. The line likely reflects a guardian telling someone not to order Yuna to summon.

text: 汝の思いは鋼より硬い。 / ロンゾの強者が束になろうと、
translation: Your resolve is harder than steel. / Even if the strongest Ronso were to band together,

vocabulary.meaning: to band together, to combine forces

grammar: 〜より硬い is a comparative: 'harder than ~'. 束になろうと is a concessive volitional: 'even if they were to band together'. 汝 (なんじ) marks this speech as ceremonial/solemn — likely Kelk speaking to Yuna.

text: 汝の意志は曲がらぬであろう。
translation: Your will would not bend.

vocabulary.meaning: to bend, to waver, to turn
classical negative auxiliary (literary equivalent of ない)

grammar: 曲がらぬ is a classical negative (ぬ = ない in literary register). であろう is an archaic conjectural form (だろう). Together they give a solemn, ceremonial tone appropriate for Kelk, the Ronso elder.

text: まこと、見事な覚悟である。行くがよい。
translation: Truly, a magnificent resolve. You may proceed.

vocabulary.meaning: resolve, preparedness, readiness to face a consequence
you may go, you are free to go (archaic permissive expression)

grammar: 行くがよい is a classical permissive construction (〜がよい = 'it is good that you do'), equivalent to 行っていい in modern speech. The overall register (まこと, である, がよい) marks this as formal ceremonial speech from an elder.

text: 霊法ガガゼとは、汝らを受け入れようぞ。
translation: The sacred peak Gagazet shall accept you all.

vocabulary.meaning: sacred/holy peak (a mountain revered as sacred)
to accept, to receive, to welcome

grammar: 受け入れようぞ is a volitional form (〜よう) with emphatic particle ぞ, giving the meaning 'shall surely accept'. This archaic construction underscores the solemnity of Kelk's declaration on behalf of Mt. Gagazet.

text: ありがとうございます。
translation: Thank you very much.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございます
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございます

text: 待て!
translation: Wait!
grammar: 待て is the imperative form of 待つ. The abrupt single-word command creates immediate dramatic tension as the party is halted.

text: まだ邪魔するってのかよ / 召喚師は通す / ガードも通す
translation: You're still going to get in the way? / The summoner may pass. / The guardians may pass too.

vocabulary.meaning: to obstruct, to get in the way
are you saying that ~? (rough/confrontational rhetorical question)
to let pass, to allow through

grammar: 〜するってのかよ is a casual/rough rhetorical question combining quotation って + のか (asking for clarification) + よ (male emphatic particle). 召喚師は通す omits the subject — the Ronso are declaring who they will allow through.

text: キマリは通さない / キマリはロンゾの面汚し
translation: Kimahri will not be allowed through. / Kimahri is a disgrace to the Ronso.

vocabulary.meaning: to let pass, to allow through

grammar: 通さない is the negative plain form of 通す. 面汚し is a compound noun (面 face + 汚し disgrace/stain) used as a harsh insult. The は topic marker singles out Kimahri for special condemnation.

text: ロンゾの使命を捨てた者 / 一族を捨て、御山も捨てた
translation: One who abandoned the Ronso's mission. / You abandoned the clan, abandoned the sacred mountain too.

vocabulary.meaning: to abandon, to throw away, to forsake
the sacred mountain (honorific お/御 + 山)

grammar: ロンゾの使命を捨てた者 is a noun phrase with a relative clause (捨てた modifies 者). The repetition of 捨て / 捨てた emphasizes Kimahri's multiple abandonments as an accusation. 御山 (おやま) uses the honorific prefix for the sacred Mt. Gagazet.

text: 小さい論図、弱い論図
translation: Little Kimahri, weak Kimahri.
grammar: 論図 (ロンゾ) here is written in kanji as a taunt — Biran and Yenke are directly insulting Kimahri by calling him small and weak. The repeated noun structure (小さい〇〇、弱い〇〇) is a rhythmic taunting pattern.

text: 御山は弱く小さいものを嫌う
translation: The sacred mountain abhors the weak and small.

vocabulary.meaning: to dislike, to abhor, to reject

grammar: 弱く小さいもの uses the adverbial form 弱く (weak → weakly/being weak) connecting two adjectives before the noun もの (thing/one). The subject is 御山 — the mountain itself is personified as rejecting the unworthy.

text: 登りたければ / 力を示せばいいのだな
translation: If you want to climb, / then all you need to do is show your strength, right?

vocabulary.meaning: all you have to do is ~, it's fine if you ~

grammar: 登りたければ is a conditional of the たい-form (want to): 〜たい + ければ = 'if you want to ~'. 力を示せばいいのだな combines conditional 〜ば + いい (it's good/sufficient) + のだ (explanatory) + な (confirmation-seeking). Kimahri is affirming the condition for being allowed to pass.

text: 勝てると思うか
translation: Do you think you can win?

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to win (potential form of 勝つ)

grammar: 勝てる is the potential form of 勝つ (to win). 〜と思うか is a question using the quotation particle と + 思う: 'do you think [that]~?'. The か without rising intonation is a sharp, challenging rhetorical question.

text: 誰がキマリの角を追ったか忘れてはいまい / キマリは一度もヴィラン隊形に勝てなかった
translation: You haven't forgotten who it was that knocked off Kimahri's horn, have you? / Kimahri has never once been able to beat Biran and Yenke.

vocabulary.meaning: to chase off, to drive away; here: to break/knock off
surely (you) haven't ~, you can't have ~ (classical negative conjecture)

grammar: 忘れてはいまい uses classical negative conjecture い (まい = will not), with the pattern 〜てはいまい meaning 'surely has not ~'. 一度も〜なかった is an emphatic negative: 'not even once'. ヴィラン is the Ronso pair Biran and Yenke, referred to by their group name.

text: 今度は勝つ / 勝つと決めた
translation: This time I will win. / I have decided to win.
grammar: 勝つと決めた uses the quotation particle と with 決める: 'decided [that I will] win'. The past tense 決めた signals this is not a new decision but a resolve already made — Kimahri's commitment is firm.

text: こんな… / ロンゾの問題だってのかよ
translation: This... / Are you saying this is a Ronso matter?

vocabulary.meaning: are you saying it's ~? (rough rhetorical question)

grammar: 〜だってのかよ is a casual/irritated rhetorical construction: だ (copula) + って (quotative) + の (nominalization/question) + か (question) + よ (male emphasis). The speaker (Tidus or Wakka) is frustrated that the group can't interfere.

text: キマリの問題だ
translation: It's Kimahri's matter.
grammar: A terse declarative sentence (noun + だ). The brevity is deliberate — likely Auron cutting off the conversation with a flat statement of fact.

text: ヴィランがやつ先にしてくれよ
translation: Let Biran go first.

vocabulary.meaning: first, ahead (lit. 'ahead of that one'; archaic/rough)
please do ~ (casual request with mild demand)

grammar: 〜してくれよ is a casual request: する (do) + くれ (give me the favor) + よ (emphasis). The construction asks someone to do something as a favor to the speaker.

text: 角なし、角なし!
translation: No horn! No horn!
grammar: 角なし is a noun + なし (without/lacking) construction. The repetition serves as a mocking chant — Biran and Yenke taunting Kimahri about his broken horn, which they themselves broke.

text: おはようございます / くんっ
translation: Good morning. / Ngh!

vocabulary.meaning: grunt/groan sound (sound of impact or exertion)

grammar: おはようございます mid-battle is dark or ironic humor. くんっ is an onomatopoeic expression of physical strain or taking a hit.

text: か、乾杯だ
translation: H-here's to you.
grammar: か, at the start indicates a stammer or surprised interjection. 乾杯だ as a battle phrase is ironic/gallows humor — the speaker acknowledges being beaten while maintaining bravado.

text: 強くなったな、キマリン
translation: You've gotten stronger, Kimahri.

vocabulary.meaning: you have ~, haven't you (past tense + な for reflection)

grammar: 強くなった is 強い (strong) in its adverbial form + なる (to become) in past tense. The な at the end is a reflective/admiring particle — Biran acknowledging Kimahri's growth with genuine respect. キマリン is an affectionate diminutive of キマリ.

text: ヴィランは嬉しいぞ
translation: Biran is glad.
grammar: ヴィラン (Biran) refers to himself in the third person — common in FFX's Ronso speech pattern. ぞ is a masculine emphatic sentence-final particle. The sentence conveys genuine joy that Kimahri has grown strong enough to defeat him.

text: 霊峰ガガゼトよ
translation: O sacred peak Gagazet,
grammar: よ used after a proper noun is a vocative particle — calling out to or addressing the mountain directly. This begins a ceremonial address, possibly from Biran (dying) dedicating something to Gagazet.

text: ヴィランを任した強者の 生えある名前を伝えよう
translation: Let me tell you the name of the mighty warrior who surpassed Biran — a name with glory.

vocabulary.meaning: to surpass, to entrust, to leave to (here: to surpass/best)
to convey, to pass on, to tell

grammar: ヴィランを任した is a relative clause modifying 強者: 'the warrior who surpassed Biran'. 生えある名前 = 'a name bearing glory'. 伝えよう is volitional (let me/let us tell). This is Biran's dying speech honoring Kimahri.

text: しかとを覚えよ!ガガゼトよ! その名は、キマリ・ロンゾなり!
translation: Remember it well! O Gagazet! That name is — Kimahri Ronso!

vocabulary.meaning: is (classical copula, equivalent to だ/です)

grammar: 覚えよ is the classical imperative of 覚える (remember!). 〜なり is a classical copula used for solemn declarations. The scene is Biran's dying tribute — he calls on Mt. Gagazet to enshrine Kimahri's name in its memory.

text: 本山はキマリの強さを知った。 キマリを受け入れるだろう。
translation: The sacred mountain now knows Kimahri's strength. It will accept Kimahri.
grammar: 知った is the past tense of 知る, signifying the mountain has now come to know. 受け入れるだろう is a conjecture with だろう. Note how Biran refers to Kimahri in the third person throughout — typical of Ronso speech patterns in FFX.

text: 召喚し、寺院からの手は、 我らロンゾが食い止める。
translation: The hands reaching from the temples after the summoner — we Ronso will hold them back.

vocabulary.meaning: hands; here: agents, forces reaching out
to hold back, to check, to stop

grammar: 寺院からの手 uses からの to create a noun-modifying phrase: 'the hands from the temples'. 食い止める is a compound verb: 食い (bite/stop) + 止める (stop). 我らロンゾ is an emphatic subject — 'we, the Ronso'. This is the Ronso's pledge to guard the party's rear.

text: 本当ですか? / 昔、キマリの角を追った償いだ
translation: Is that true? / It is atonement for breaking Kimahri's horn long ago.

vocabulary.meaning: to knock off, to chase away; here: to break off

grammar: 昔、キマリの角を追った償いだ — 追った is relative clause modifying 償い: 'atonement for [what was done] — breaking Kimahri's horn'. だ is a plain declarative. The Ronso's pledge is framed as making amends for their past cruelty.

text: 召喚師の後ろから来る敵は我らが倒す
translation: Enemies that come from behind the summoner — we will defeat them.
grammar: 召喚師の後ろから来る敵 is a relative clause noun phrase: 'enemies that come from behind the summoner'. は marks it as the topic. 我らが倒す uses が for emphasis on the subject (we will be the ones to defeat them).

text: ユーナの前に立つ敵はキマリが倒す / お前ほど恵まれた召喚師はいない
translation: Enemies that stand before Yuna — Kimahri will defeat them. / There is no summoner as blessed as you.

vocabulary.meaning: to be blessed, to be fortunate

grammar: お前ほど恵まれた召喚師はいない uses the degree marker ほど in a negative comparison: 'there is no summoner as blessed as you'. This construction (〜ほど〜はいない) expresses superlative praise.

text: ありがとうございます / お前の像ができたらロンゾが磨いてやる
translation: Thank you very much. / When your statue is made, the Ronso will polish it.

vocabulary.meaning: to be made, to be completed, to be ready
to polish, to buff, to shine
to do (something) for someone (casual, slightly patronizing but warm)

grammar: 〜たらロンゾが磨いてやる: たら is a conditional 'when/if'. 磨いてやる is the て-form + やる (to do for someone from above). From the Ronso, this is a warm, slightly gruff gesture of loyalty — not condescension.

text: でも、私は反逆者ですから、きっと像は作ってもらえません
translation: But since I am a rebel, surely no statue will be made for me.

vocabulary.meaning: to have (something) made for one (potential of もらう)

grammar: 〜てもらえません is the negative potential of 〜てもらう (to have someone do something for you): 'cannot have [a statue] made'. ですから gives a polite explanation. Yuna is matter-of-factly accepting that as a rebel against Yevon, she won't receive official honors.

text: ならば、ロンゾが作る
translation: Then the Ronso will make one.

vocabulary.meaning: if that is the case, then (formal conditional)

grammar: ならば is a formal conditional ('if that is so, then'). The subject ロンゾが is emphatic — the Ronso themselves will take on this task. The brevity of the sentence conveys firm resolve.

text: 立派な角をつけてやる
translation: We'll give it a fine horn.

vocabulary.meaning: to do for someone (warm, slightly assertive)

grammar: 立派な角をつけてやる — the horn is symbolically important because Yuna is human (no horn). The Ronso will give her statue a Ronso horn as an honor. てやる again shows warm, gruff generosity.

text: はい、お願いします
translation: Yes, please.

text: 俺も、ユーナの像を見上げたいと思った。ユーナと一緒にさ。
translation: I thought I wanted to look up at Yuna's statue too. Together with Yuna.
grammar: 〜たいと思った is past tense: 'thought I wanted to ~', suggesting a fleeting wish that may not come true. ユーナと一緒にさ is a trailing afterthought with さ — Tidus's inner voice, wistful and bittersweet, knowing Yuna won't survive the journey.

text: 山越えたら、ジャナルカンドだよ。
translation: Once we cross the mountain, it's Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: to cross over, to get past

grammar: 〜たら here is a temporal conditional: 'once we cross'. だよ is a casual affirmative assertion. The weight in this line is contextual — Zanarkand means the end of the journey and Yuna's death.

text: 分かってる。
translation: I know.
grammar: 分かってる is the て-form + いる contracted to てる, indicating an ongoing state of knowing. The brevity signals that the speaker (Yuna) understands the implication fully and doesn't need elaboration.

text: ユーナ、究極召喚手に入れちゃうよ。 / 分かってるよ。
translation: Yuna, you're going to get the Final Summoning. / I know.

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん
vocabulary.meaning: Final Summoning (the ultimate summoning that defeats Sin, at the cost of the summoner's life)
to obtain, to get one's hands on
to end up doing ~ (colloquial contraction of 〜てしまう)

grammar: 〜ちゃうよ is a contraction of 〜てしまうよ: 'you're going to end up getting/doing ~'. The てしまう often implies an irreversible or regrettable outcome — Tidus knows obtaining 究極召喚 means Yuna's death. 分かってるよ echoes the previous line with added よ for emotional emphasis.

text: 私…なんも思いつかない / 俺もだ
translation: I... can't think of anything. / Me neither.

vocabulary.meaning: nothing at all (dialectal/colloquial variant of 何も)
to think of, to come up with an idea

grammar: なんも is a colloquial/dialectal form of 何も (nothing). 思いつかない is the negative of 思いつく (to think of/come up with). 俺もだ is a short elliptical response: 'me too [can't think of anything]'.

text: どうしよう
translation: What should we do?

vocabulary.meaning: what to do, how to handle it

grammar: どうしよう is a common expression of uncertainty or being at a loss: 'what shall we do / what are we going to do'. The volitional form (しよう vs. すればいい) gives it an open, unresolved feeling.

text: なんとかなる!今の俺たちは何も知らない / このままじゃ、ユーナを助けられないけど
translation: We'll figure something out! Right now we don't know anything. / As things stand, we can't save Yuna, but—

vocabulary.meaning: things will work out somehow, it'll be fine
as things are, at this rate
to save, to help, to rescue

grammar: なんとかなる is a set phrase of optimism. このままじゃ is a conditional: 'if things stay like this' (このまま + では contracted to じゃ). けど at the end leaves the sentence trailing — a 'but...' that signals Tidus has a plan coming.

text: ザナルカンドへ行こう! / 行けば何かわかるって
translation: Let's go to Zanarkand! / If we go, we'll figure something out.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm telling you, you know (casual quotative/assertion particle)

grammar: 行こう is the volitional form: 'let's go'. 行けば何かわかるって uses conditional 行けば + わかる (will understand/know) + って (casual assertive quotation, expressing confidence). Tidus is rallying the group with conviction.

text: きっと、そこから始まるんだ
translation: I'm sure that's where it all begins.
grammar: きっと expresses strong conviction. 〜んだ (contracted from のだ) adds an explanatory or assertive tone — Tidus is not just speculating but declaring his belief. そこから (from there) suggests the answer/solution will emerge at Zanarkand.

text: へぇ…
translation: Hmm...

vocabulary.meaning: huh, oh, I see (expression of mild surprise or being impressed)

grammar: へぇ is an interjection conveying mild surprise or being impressed. The trailing … suggests the speaker (likely Rikku or Yuna) is processing what Tidus said.

text: 今、頼れるエースって感じしたよ
translation: Just now you felt like a real ace I can rely on.

vocabulary.meaning: to be reliable, to be dependable (potential of 頼る)

grammar: 頼れるエース is a relative clause: 'an ace who can be relied upon'. 〜って感じがした is a common pattern: 'had the feeling of being ~'. Rikku is complimenting Tidus on sounding confident and dependable for once.

text: 最初から言ってんだろ?
translation: Haven't I been saying that from the start?

vocabulary.meaning: haven't been ~ing? (contracted ている + んだろう, seeking agreement)

grammar: 言ってんだろ is a contraction of 言っているんだろう: 言って (te-form) + いる (ongoing) + んだ (emphatic) + ろ (rhetorical question). Tidus is mock-boasting that he told them so.

text: ははー!
translation: Ha ha!

text: ほう、ジェクトの息子か / リュック、先に行ってアーロンに伝えろ
translation: Oh, so you're Jecht's son. / Rikku, go ahead and tell Auron.

vocabulary.meaning: oh, I see (expression of mild surprise or recognition)
to go ahead, to go first
to convey, to tell, to pass on

grammar: ジェクトの息子か uses か as a recognition-question ('so you're ~?'), not seeking information but processing a realization. 伝えろ is the rough imperative form of 伝える — Tidus is commanding Rikku urgently.

text: 一人で戦う気? / いいから行けって!
translation: You're going to fight alone? / Just go already!

vocabulary.meaning: intention, feeling, mood (〜する気 = intention to do ~)
just do it, never mind that, it's fine so (dismissive)
I said ~ (quotative for repeating/emphasizing one's own command)

grammar: 〜する気? drops the copula (〜する気がある?) for casual shortness: 'are you intending to ~?'. いいから行けって uses いいから (dismissive 'it's fine, just') + 行け (imperative) + って (quotative emphasis — 'I said go!'). Tidus brushing off Rikku's concern.

text: よかろう 死の安息に沈ね
translation: Very well. Sink into the peace of death.

vocabulary.meaning: very well, so be it (archaic conjectural/permissive of よい)

grammar: よかろう is classical: the volitional/conjectural of よい (よかろう = 'it shall be fine/so be it'). 沈ね: 沈む in its classical imperative form (む → め → ね is archaic imperative). The line is Seymour commanding Tidus to die — framed in deliberately ornate, deathly language.

text: つかしてんじゃねえよ! / 発光をつけるな!
translation: Stop fooling around! / Don't use that light!

vocabulary.word: つかしてんじゃねえよ
vocabulary.reading: つかしてんじゃねえよ
vocabulary.meaning: stop messing around, don't screw with me (rough colloquial)

grammar: 〜してんじゃねえよ is a rough negative command: している + じゃない + よ, contracted. つけるな is a plain negative imperative (don't attach/turn on). Both lines reflect the urgency and roughness of the battle moment.

text: ユーナ殿 お久しゅう / ユーナ!
translation: Lady Yuna, it has been a while. / Yuna!

vocabulary.meaning: it has been a long time (archaic/formal variant of お久しぶり)

grammar: 〜殿 (どの) is a formal honorific used in historical or ceremonial contexts. お久しゅう is an archaic contraction of お久しぶりです, using the classical 〜く → 〜う sound shift. This is Seymour greeting Yuna with cold formality.

text: ふん、異界送りか / その前にロンゾの生き残りに伝えたいことがある
translation: Hmph, a Sending, is it? / Before that, there is something I want to convey to the Ronso survivors.

vocabulary.meaning: the Sending (ritual to send the dead to the Farplane)

grammar: 異界送りか: the か here signals recognition/realization ('so it's a Sending?'). その前に introduces a temporal condition: 'before that'. 伝えたいことがある is a polite but ominous way of saying 'there is something I wish to say' — Seymour is stalling or making a point before his death rite.

text: ふんふんふん
translation: Hmm hmm hmm.

vocabulary.meaning: hmm hmm hmm (self-satisfied chuckling or contemplative humming)

grammar: Seymour's characteristic cold, amused vocalization — conveying contempt or smug satisfaction.

text: 実は、実に勇敢な一族が
translation: Actually, there was a truly brave clan —

vocabulary.meaning: actually, in fact, to tell the truth

grammar: 実は introduces a revelation or confession. 実に is an intensifying adverb ('truly/indeed'). The sentence is unfinished — trailing into the next clip. Seymour is setting up his account of what he did to the Ronso.

text: 私の行く手を阻もうと捨て身で挑みかかり
translation: That threw itself at me with reckless abandon, trying to block my path,

vocabulary.meaning: one's path ahead, the way forward
to block, to obstruct, to hinder
reckless abandon, self-sacrifice (lit. 'throwing away one's body')
to challenge, to attack, to throw oneself at

grammar: 〜もうと is a volitional + と: 'trying to ~'. 捨て身で is an adverbial manner phrase. 挑みかかり is the 連用形 (stem) of 挑みかかる used as a connective — the sentence continues. Seymour is describing the Ronso attack with a mixture of cold admiration and cruelty.

text: 一人、また一人
translation: One by one, and then another.
grammar: 一人、また一人 is a rhythmic repetition implying a sequence: Seymour killed the Ronso one after another. The elliptical structure (no verb) forces the listener to complete the horrific image themselves.

text: ふっふっふっ わかない / キマリ
translation: Heh heh heh — [I wiped them out.] / Kimahri.

vocabulary.meaning: unclear in isolation — possibly 若い (young) or a distortion; contextually the Ronso were eliminated

grammar: The laugh is Seymour's signature cold amusement. キマリ as a standalone word at the end may be Seymour calling to Kimahri directly, pivoting the cruelty of the story toward him personally.

text: そのロンゾの悲しみ 癒してやりたくはないと
translation: Wouldn't you want to heal that sorrow of the Ronso?

vocabulary.meaning: to heal, to soothe, to relieve

grammar: 癒してやりたくはないと: 癒す + てやる (do for) + たい (want) + は (topic/emphasis) + ない (negative) + と (quotative/rhetorical). The negative question 〜たくはないと is Seymour's manipulative rhetorical appeal — 'Don't you want to ease the Ronso's pain?' — as justification for his genocidal mercy killing logic.

text: 何を言いたいのです
translation: What is it you are trying to say?

vocabulary.meaning: want to say (たい-form of 言う)

grammar: 何を言いたいのです is a polite but direct challenge: 'what is it you want to say?'. のです adds a demand for explanation. Yuna is not intimidated and is cutting straight to the point.

text: 彼を死なせてやればいい 悲しみはつゆと消える
translation: Just let him die — the sorrow will vanish like morning dew.

vocabulary.meaning: to let die, to cause to die (causative of 死ぬ)
all you have to do is ~ (for someone)
dew (morning dew — poetic image of something ephemeral)

grammar: 死なせてやればいい: causative 死なせる + てやる (do for) + ばいい (all that's needed). Seymour frames Kimahri's death as mercy. つゆと消える is a literary simile — 'disappear like dew'. Seymour's language is consistently poetic and detached, masking cruelty in beauty.

text: スピナ 死の螺旋に囚われた
translation: Spira, bound in a spiral of death.

vocabulary.meaning: to be trapped, to be bound, to be imprisoned

grammar: 死の螺旋 is a metaphor central to FFX's mythology — Spira is trapped in an endless cycle of Sin's destruction and temporary peace. 囚われた is the passive past of 囚われる: 'was/has been bound'. Seymour is building his philosophical justification.

text: 悲しみと苦しみの大地 / すべて滅ぼして癒すために
translation: A land of sorrow and suffering. / In order to heal it by destroying it all.

vocabulary.meaning: to destroy, to annihilate, to wipe out
in order to ~, for the purpose of ~

grammar: すべて滅ぼして癒すために: すべて (all) + 滅ぼして (destroy, te-form connecting to 癒す) + ために (purpose clause). Seymour's twisted logic: destroy everything to heal the pain of existence. The ために clause signals this as his stated goal.

text: 私は真になる
translation: I will become Sin.
grammar: 真 (シン/Sin) is written here with the kanji for 'truth/genuine' — a deliberate double meaning. Seymour declares his intention to become Sin himself. 〜になる (to become) marks a transformation goal. This is the crux of his plan.

text: あなたの力によって
translation: By your power.

vocabulary.meaning: by means of, through, due to

grammar: によって marks the means or agent. The sentence is a fragment — Seymour is building his speech dramatically, leaving the main clause for the next line.

text: 私と共に来るがよ
translation: Come with me.

vocabulary.meaning: you should, it would be good if you (archaic/formal command)

grammar: 〜がよい is an archaic imperative form, giving Seymour's speech a grand, imperious tone. More formal and haughty than 来い or 来てください.

text: 私が新たな真となれば
translation: If I become the new Sin,

vocabulary.meaning: Sin (the creature); also means 'truth' — a deliberate pun in Seymour's rhetoric

grammar: 〜となれば is a conditional: と (result marker) + なれば (conditional of なる). The sentence is left open — the consequence follows in the next line.

text: お前の父も救われるのだ
translation: Your father too will be saved.

vocabulary.meaning: to be saved, to be rescued (passive of 救う)

grammar: 救われる is the passive form of 救う. のだ adds an explanatory, assertive nuance — Seymour is presenting this as a logical conclusion Tidus should accept.

text: お前に何がわかるってんだ!
translation: What the hell do you know about it!

vocabulary.meaning: contracted form of というんだ — 'what is this about...?', used angrily

grammar: お前に〜がわかる uses に to mark the experiencer of understanding. ってんだ is a contracted colloquial form of というんだ, expressing frustration or disbelief. This is Tidus snapping at Seymour.

text: 哀れなものだ
translation: How pitiful.

vocabulary.meaning: how ~ it is (expresses an emotional judgment)

grammar: 哀れなものだ is a set expression of contempt or condescension: 'what a pitiful thing.' Seymour dismisses Tidus's anger coolly.

text: だが、その絶望もここで消えた
translation: But that despair too ends here.

vocabulary.meaning: to disappear, to vanish, to be extinguished

grammar: もここで places both the focus particle も ('also') and the location で ('at this place'). Seymour uses the past tense 消えた as if it has already been decided — a rhetorical technique projecting inevitability.

text: 全ての嘆きを発揮するもの
translation: The one who unleashes all lament —

vocabulary.meaning: to unleash, to demonstrate, to bring out fully

grammar: 発揮する typically means 'to display/bring out (a quality).' Here Seymour uses it dramatically to mean 'to bring forth/unleash.' 〜もの nominalizes the clause, referring to Seymour himself as the one who fulfills this role. This line begins his battle invocation before Seymour Flux.

text: もう邪魔すんなよ!
translation: Stop getting in our way already!

vocabulary.meaning: already; (with negatives) anymore; (with commands) enough of this
to interfere, to obstruct, to get in the way
don't do (contracted colloquial form of するな)

grammar: すんな is a contracted colloquial negative imperative from するな. Combined with よ, it expresses exasperated frustration. This is after the Seymour Flux battle.

text: 私の力でシンになる / 戯言だ、忘れろ
translation: He'll become Sin through my power. / Nonsense — forget it.
grammar: Two speakers: Tidus reports what Seymour said (私の力で = through my [Yuna's] power, Seymour would become Sin). Auron dismisses it curtly with 戯言だ, 忘れろ — bare imperative form of 忘れる, very direct.

text: 彼がシンになれば、ジェクトさんが救われる
translation: If he becomes Sin, Jecht will be saved.
grammar: Conditional ば-form: 〜になれば introduces the condition. The implication is that Jecht, currently trapped inside Sin, would be released if Seymour took over as Sin. Tidus is beginning to process this out loud.

text: 行くぞ / 何か知ってるなら教えてください
translation: Let's go. / If you know something, please tell me.
grammar: 行くぞ is a strong volitional with ぞ, typically masculine — Auron urging them forward. 〜なら is a conditional ('if'). ください makes the request polite; Yuna is appealing to Auron.

text: 教えて
translation: Please, tell me.

vocabulary.meaning: to tell, to teach, to inform

grammar: Short te-form request 教えて without ください — more emotionally direct and urgent than the polite form. Yuna is pleading.

text: シン / 親父なんだ
translation: Sin… is my dad.

vocabulary.meaning: dad, old man (casual, masculine term for father)

grammar: Tidus blurts out the revelation. なんだ (< のだ) here signals a confession or explanation of something Tidus has been holding back. The pause between シン and 親父なんだ mirrors emotional difficulty.

text: なんだそりゃ / シンは俺の親父だ
translation: What's that supposed to mean? / Sin is my father.

vocabulary.meaning: What is that? What are you talking about? (colloquial, surprised)

grammar: なんだそりゃ is a contracted colloquial expression from なんだそれは, expressing shock or disbelief. Then Tidus rephrases more clearly with the plain assertive だ: シンは俺の親父だ.

text: 親父がシンになったんだ
translation: My dad became Sin.
grammar: 〜になったんだ combines the past tense of なる with explanatory のだ. Tidus is clarifying and explaining the situation, not just stating a fact.

text: 理屈とかそういうのよくわからない
translation: I don't really understand the logic or whatever.

vocabulary.meaning: things like ~, that kind of stuff
don't really understand, can't quite grasp

grammar: とか lists examples loosely (similar to 'or whatever'), and そういうの is a nominalizer meaning 'that kind of thing.' よく before a negative softens/hedges: 'not very well / not really.'

text: でも俺
translation: But me, I…
grammar: A trailing fragment — Tidus starts a sentence that he finishes in the next clip. でも sets up a contrast with his admission of not understanding the logic.

text: シンの中には… / 親父がいる
translation: Inside Sin… my dad is there.
grammar: 〜の中には uses the compound particle には for location with contrast/emphasis. いる (not ある) because Jecht is a person. The ellipsis and pause between clauses conveys Tidus struggling to say this.

text: 親父がスピラーを苦しめてるんだ / ごめん
translation: My dad is the one tormenting Spira. / I'm sorry.

vocabulary.meaning: to torment, to cause suffering, to afflict
is doing (ongoing) — explanatory のだ with progressive て-form

grammar: 〜ているんだ combines the progressive form (てる = ている contracted) with explanatory のだ. Tidus feels personally responsible for his father's actions — hence the apology ごめん.

text: ごめん
translation: I'm sorry.
grammar: Repeated apology for emphasis. ごめん is the casual form of ごめんなさい. Tidus repeating it underscores his guilt and emotional weight.

text: たとえ… / シンがジェクトさんでも…
translation: Even if… Sin is Jecht…

vocabulary.meaning: even if, no matter how (used with ~ても/~でも)
even if it is ~, even though ~ (concessive)

grammar: たとえ〜でも is a set concessive structure: 'even if ~ is the case.' Yuna begins to say something difficult — that even knowing Sin is Jecht, she cannot stop her mission. She trails off before completing the thought.

text: シンがシンである限り…私…
translation: As long as Sin is Sin… I…

vocabulary.meaning: as long as ~ is ~, so long as

grammar: 〜である限り is a formal conditional: 'as long as X exists as X.' The repetition of シン (Sin is Sin) is rhetorically powerful — Sin's nature as a threat does not change regardless of who inhabits it. Yuna's ellipsis shows she cannot finish the sentence aloud.

text: わかってる / 倒そう / 親父もそれを望んでる / 父親と戦える
translation: I know. / Let's defeat him. / Dad wants that too. / I can fight my own father.

vocabulary.meaning: I know, I understand (progressive — I'm in a state of knowing)
can fight, is able to fight (potential form of 戦う)

grammar: 倒そう is volitional ('let's'). 〜ている for 望む: 望んでいる = is wishing/wanting, contracted to 望んでる. 戦える is the potential form — Tidus reassuring himself and Yuna that he is capable of fighting his father.

text: 大丈夫
translation: It's okay.
grammar: Single-word reassurance, no verb needed. The brevity itself carries emotional weight — Tidus reassuring Yuna (and himself) with just these two words.

text: やるよ / 俺 / なあその話よ
translation: I'll do it. / Me. / Hey, about that story —

vocabulary.meaning: to do, to go ahead with (casual, determined)

grammar: やるよ uses よ for assertion. 俺 alone as emphasis — 'it's me who will do it.' なあ signals a topic shift; someone (Wakka) is steering to what was just revealed.

text: 真の毒家にやられて夢を見た / わけじゃねえよな
translation: I didn't just get hit by Sin's toxin and dream all that up, right?

vocabulary.meaning: Sin's toxin/poison (Sin Trance — the hallucinogenic effect of Sin's proximity)
to be done in by, to be affected by, to be hit
to have a dream, to dream
it's not the case that ~, right? (seeking confirmation)

grammar: わけじゃない means 'it's not the case that ~.' ねえ is a colloquial contraction of ない. よな adds a seeking-agreement nuance: 'that's not it, right?' Wakka is processing what he just heard and checking if it was real.

text: じゃあチャップ
translation: So then, chap —

vocabulary.meaning: chap, buddy (Wakka's casual address to Tidus)

grammar: じゃあ transitions to a new question or implication. チャップ (from English 'chap') is Wakka's characteristic nickname for Tidus. The sentence is left incomplete — interrupted or trailing off.

text: 悪いけどよ / 俺何も聞いてないことにしとくか
translation: Sorry man, but… I'm gonna pretend I didn't hear any of that.

vocabulary.meaning: sorry, but; I hate to say it, but (apologetic preface)
to decide to treat it as ~, to make it that ~
to do and leave it in that state, to do in advance

grammar: 聞いてないことにしとく combines: 聞いていない (haven't heard) + ことにする (treat as if) + ておく contracted to とく. Wakka is humorously deciding to process the overwhelming information by ignoring it for now.

text: 頭こんがらがってきたぞ
translation: My head's starting to get all tangled up.

vocabulary.meaning: to get tangled, to get confused, to get mixed up
has come to ~, is beginning to ~ (gradual change)

grammar: こんがらがる is an expressive verb for mental confusion/entanglement. 〜てきた indicates a process that has been developing and is now manifest. ぞ adds a self-directed assertion.

text: なんでまたそんなことになっちまったんだ
translation: How in the world did things end up like this?

vocabulary.meaning: such a thing, something like that
ended up becoming (colloquial contraction of になってしまった)

grammar: になっちまった is contracted from になってしまった, expressing an unfortunate or unwanted result. んだ adds the explanatory/questioning nuance. Wakka is expressing bewildered frustration at the whole situation.

text: 行けばわかる / もうすぐだ
translation: Go there and you'll understand. / We're almost there.
grammar: 行けば is the conditional ば-form of 行く: 'if you go.' わかる follows naturally as the result. Auron's characteristic terseness — no wasted words. もうすぐだ states they're almost at Zanarkand.

text: なんだこれ / 祈り御様だよ
translation: What is this? / These are the fayth.

vocabulary.meaning: fayth (beings who lend their power to summoners)

grammar: なんだこれ inverts the standard こそあど word order (これはなんだ) for emphatic surprise — typical of spoken Japanese. 祈り御様 is a respectful form; the speaker adds 御〜様 out of reverence for the fayth.

text: 召喚されてる 誰かが召喚してる
translation: They're being summoned. Someone is summoning them.
grammar: 召喚されてる is passive progressive (召喚されている contracted): 'are being summoned.' Then active: 誰かが召喚してる — someone is actively summoning them. The distinction passive/active shows Lulu analyzing the situation.

text: この祈り子様たちから力を引き出してる / こんなにいっぱい? / 波外れた力ね 一体誰が…何を…
translation: They're drawing power from all these fayth. / This many? / What extraordinary power… just who… for what…

vocabulary.meaning: this many, so many of them

grammar: 引き出してる is progressive (している contracted). 波外れた modifies 力: 'extraordinary power.' 一体 intensifies question words (who, what) to convey disbelief. The trailing ellipses show Lulu trailing off in awe.

text: ねぇ! なんか知ってるんでしょ?
translation: Hey! You know something, don't you?

vocabulary.meaning: to know (progressive — to be in a state of knowing)
you do, don't you? (accusatory rhetorical question)

grammar: 〜んでしょ (< のでしょう) is a rhetorical confirmation-seeking question that implies the speaker already suspects the answer is yes. Rikku is confronting Auron, who always seems to know more than he reveals.

text: 教えてよ! / 他人の知識などあてにするな 何のための旅だ
translation: Tell us! / Don't rely on others' knowledge. What was this journey for?

vocabulary.meaning: to rely on ~ (など is dismissive: 'such things as')
what is it for, for what purpose

grammar: あてにするな is a negative imperative (するな). など is dismissive, downplaying what it modifies. Auron's rhetorical question 何のための旅だ challenges them to use what they've learned on the journey themselves.

text: ユーナンの命がかかってるんだよ! / いや、アーロンの言う通りだ。
translation: Yuna's life is on the line! / No — Auron is right.

vocabulary.meaning: is at stake, is hanging on (かかる = to be at stake)

grammar: 命がかかっている is an idiomatic expression: 'one's life is at stake.' 〜んだよ adds emotional emphasis (のだ + よ). いや concedes the prior objection; 言う通りだ agrees: 'what Auron says is correct.'

text: えっ? / これは俺たち、
translation: Huh? / This is our —
grammar: Tidus begins a sentence he finishes in the next clip. えっ is Rikku's or another character's surprised response to Tidus siding with Auron.

text: 俺の物語なんだから。
translation: Because this is my story.

vocabulary.meaning: because it is ~ (explanatory のだ + から for reasoning)

grammar: なんだから combines the explanatory のだ with the causal から: 'because this is [my] story.' This is one of FFX's thematic lines — Tidus asserting ownership over his own narrative destiny. The から provides the reason he must face it himself.

text: うわっ!
translation: Whoa!
grammar: Pure exclamation — Tidus is surprised/startled, likely as he is pulled into the vision of the fayth.

text: おかえり
translation: Welcome back.

vocabulary.meaning: welcome back, welcome home (greeting for someone returning)

grammar: おかえり is the standard greeting for someone returning home, short for おかえりなさい. The fayth boy uses it to greet Tidus as if this space — the dream of Zanarkand — is his home.

text: お前… / ベベルで会ったよ。覚えてる?
translation: You… / We met in Bevelle. Remember?

vocabulary.meaning: to remember (progressive — to be in a state of remembering)

grammar: The fayth boy confirms their prior meeting. 覚えてる is the progressive of 覚える: 'do you retain the memory?' The question is genuine — Tidus encountered the fayth in Bevelle earlier.

text: あ…ああ… / けど、あれが最初じゃないよね。
translation: Ah… yeah… / But that wasn't the first time, was it.

vocabulary.meaning: it's not ~, right? (seeking confirmation of a negative)

grammar: じゃないよね combines the negative じゃない with よね (seeking agreement). Tidus is realizing he has a longer, deeper connection to this fayth — from before the game began.

text: 君のことを前から知ってる。きっと…ずっと昔から…
translation: I've known you for a long time. Surely… from long, long ago…

vocabulary.meaning: about ~, regarding ~ (marks a person as the object of knowledge/feelings)
for a long time, from before
long, long ago, from way back

grammar: 〜のことを知っている is the standard pattern for 'to know a person.' 前から indicates the knowledge has existed from before now. ずっと intensifies 昔: 'way back.' The trailing ellipsis implies the fayth's knowledge stretches back 1,000 years.

text: 俺も…知ってるような気がする。
translation: I also… feel like I know you.

vocabulary.meaning: feel like ~, have the sense that ~ (expresses uncertain feeling)

grammar: 〜ような気がする expresses a feeling or impression that isn't fully certain: 'it feels as if.' Tidus's connection to the fayth predates conscious memory, so he senses it without being able to explain it.

text: ここは? / 変なこと言うな、君の家だろ?
translation: Where is this? / Don't say something strange — it's your home, isn't it?

vocabulary.meaning: right? isn't it? (casual form of だろう)

grammar: ここは? is an abbreviated question (full: ここはどこですか?). 変なこと言うな: imperative negative. 君の家だろ: rhetorical confirmation — the fayth gently telling Tidus he belongs here in this dream Zanarkand.

text: どうしちゃったんだよ!おい!
translation: What happened to you! Hey!

vocabulary.meaning: what happened (to you), what's wrong (contraction of どうしてしまった)

grammar: どうしちゃったんだよ contracts どうしてしまったのだ: 'what has happened to you?' んだ adds the explanatory/emphatic nuance, よ adds urgency. Tidus has collapsed or entered a trance; the party is calling out to him.

text: ねえ、起きてってば!
translation: Hey, wake up already!

vocabulary.meaning: to wake up, to get up
I said ~! (emphatic repetition particle, expressing exasperation)

grammar: 〜ってば expresses that the speaker has already said something and is repeating it with frustration. 起きてってば = 'I said wake up!' Rikku is urgently trying to rouse Tidus.

text: もしかして、全部夢だろ?
translation: Could it be… it's all a dream, right?

vocabulary.meaning: could it be that, perhaps, by any chance

grammar: もしかして introduces a tentative hypothesis. Tidus is still in the vision/dream state, asking the fayth boy directly. だろ (casual だろう) seeks confirmation — Tidus suspected this but is confronting it.

text: あたり! / 夢… / ざけんなっての!
translation: Correct! / A dream… / Don't mess with me!

vocabulary.meaning: correct! hit! you're right! (from 当たり)
don't screw around, don't mess with me (vulgar contraction of ふざけるな)
emphatic colloquial ending: 'I said!' or adds force to statement

grammar: あたり is used like 'bingo!' or 'got it in one!' ざけんなっての is a strongly emphatic colloquial form of ふざけるな + という: 'stop joking around, I'm serious.' Tidus is furious at the revelation.

text: 夢なんか見てる暇ないんだからさ! / 違うよ…
translation: I don't have time to be dreaming! / No, that's not it…

vocabulary.meaning: dreaming and such, something like dreaming (なんか = dismissive)
to be different, to be wrong, that's not it

grammar: なんか is dismissive ('something as trivial as dreaming'). 〜ている暇ない: 'no time to be doing ~.' んだから adds explanation/emphasis + さ softens slightly. 違うよ is the fayth correcting Tidus.

text: 君は夢を見てるんじゃない…
translation: You aren't seeing a dream…

vocabulary.meaning: it's not that ~, you're not doing ~ (emphatic negative)

grammar: 〜んじゃない (< のではない) is an emphatic negative, correcting a mistaken assumption. The fayth is drawing the distinction between 'dreaming' and what Tidus actually is.

text: 君が夢なんだ…
translation: You are the dream…
grammar: The pivotal revelation of FFX delivered in six syllables. なんだ marks this as a deeply explanatory statement — not merely an assertion, but the explanation of everything. The subject-predicate inversion from the previous line (夢を見る → 夢である) is rhetorically elegant.

text: なんだよそれ…
translation: What does that even mean…

vocabulary.meaning: what is that (supposed to mean)? (confused, frustrated)

grammar: なんだよそれ is a colloquial inversion of それはなんだよ, expressing confusion or frustrated disbelief. よ adds emotional force. Tidus cannot process the revelation.

text: 昔、大きな戦争があった。
translation: Long ago, there was a great war.

vocabulary.meaning: long ago, in the old days

grammar: 昔 sets the temporal frame. 大きな is the prenominal form (used before nouns), contrasting with 大きい (predicative). があった is the past of ある for an event: 'there was.' The fayth begins explaining the Machina War.

text: ああ、機械の?
translation: Oh, the one with the machines?
grammar: 機械の? is an abbreviated question: 機械の(戦争)? The の links it to the implicit noun. Tidus recognizes the Machina War from Spiran history.

text: うん。ザナルカンドとベベルが戦ったんだ。
translation: Yes. Zanarkand and Bevelle went to war.

vocabulary.meaning: to fight, to go to war

grammar: 戦ったんだ: past tense + のだ (explanatory). The fayth is explaining history as it connects to Tidus's existence. が marks both Zanarkand and Bevelle as co-subjects of the war.

text: 初めから勝負はついてた。
translation: From the start, the outcome was already decided.

vocabulary.meaning: from the beginning, from the start
was already settled/decided (〜がつく = to be settled)

grammar: 勝負がつく is an idiomatic expression meaning 'the winner/loser is determined.' ついてた is the progressive past (ついていた contracted): 'was already in a decided state.' The implication: Zanarkand could not win against Bevelle's machina.

text: 召喚って、神? / 違うよ。ここだよ。眠らない町。ザナルカンド。
translation: The summoning — a god? / No. It's here. The city that never sleeps. Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: does not sleep (negative form of 眠る)

grammar: 召喚って is a topic-marking colloquialism (〜って = は): 'as for the summoning.' 違うよ simply denies. 眠らない町 is a noun phrase ('the town that doesn't sleep') — a famous epithet for Zanarkand, echoing the opening of the game.

text: 祈り子たちの夢を束ねて、町の思い出を召喚したんだ。
translation: They gathered the dreams of the fayth and summoned the memories of the city.

vocabulary.meaning: to bundle, to gather together, to unite

grammar: 束ねて is the te-form, connecting to the next action: 'gathered and then summoned.' The subject is implied (the fayth collectively). This explains the mechanism: the fayth's combined dreams sustain the dream Zanarkand.

text: 一つ一つの建物だとか、町に住んでた人とかね。
translation: Each building, and the people who lived in the city, and so on.

vocabulary.meaning: one by one, each and every one
things like ~, and ~ and so forth (listing with casual ね)

grammar: 〜だとか〜とか is a listing structure for examples ('things like A and B'). 住んでた is the contracted progressive past (住んでいた): 'who were living / used to live.' ね softens the sentence conversationally.

text: 人って、それも夢かよ。
translation: The people — are they dreams too?
grammar: 〜って is colloquial topic marker. それも uses も ('also') to extend the category to people too, not just buildings. かよ combines the question particle か with the emphatic/rough particle よ — expressing disbelief.

text: 俺も
translation: Me too.
grammar: Just two words, but carrying enormous emotional weight. Tidus realizes and states aloud that he himself is also a dream — も ('also/too') includes him in the same category as the summoned people of Zanarkand.

text: 君は祈り子たちの夢
translation: You are the dream of the fayth.

vocabulary.meaning: the fayth (plural — たち is a pluralizer)

grammar: A nominal sentence (no verb/copula needed in poetic/solemn contexts). 君は祈り子たちの夢 = 'You [are] the dream of the fayth.' The omission of だ/です gives it a weightier, more declarative quality.

text: 君のお父さんもお母さんも / みんなみんな
translation: Your father, your mother too — everyone, everyone.
grammar: も repeated with each person (お父さんも、お母さんも) indicates inclusion of each in the same category: 'also.' みんなみんな doubles for emotional intensity — 'every single one of them.'

text: 夢
translation: Dreams.
grammar: A single word completing the sequence — 'all dreams.' The starkness of the delivery (one word after the pause) makes it devastating. No copula, no explanation.

text: 祈り子たちの夢が消えたら
translation: When the dreams of the fayth fade away —

vocabulary.meaning: to disappear, to fade, to be extinguished

grammar: 〜たら is a conditional that can express both 'if' and 'when.' Here it's closer to 'when' — the fayth is speaking of something that will happen, leaving the consequence implicit (Tidus will disappear). The sentence is left unfinished, ending on たら — a rhetorical ellipsis.

text: やめろよ
translation: Stop it.

vocabulary.meaning: to stop, to quit, to cease
sentence-final particle adding emphasis or assertion

grammar: やめろ is the plain imperative of やめる. Adding よ softens it slightly while retaining urgency — Tidus is reacting emotionally to the fayth's revelation that he is a dream.

text: 夢でもなんでもいいよ / 俺を
translation: Whether I'm a dream or whatever, it doesn't matter. / Just don't—
grammar: 夢でもなんでもいいよ uses でも twice: first as 'even if (I'm a dream)' and second as part of なんでも 'whatever'. The sentence 俺を is deliberately cut off — Tidus is unable to finish the thought, building into the next line.

text: 消すな / ずっと夢を見てて
translation: Don't erase me. / Just keep on dreaming.

vocabulary.meaning: to erase, to extinguish, to make disappear
to have a dream, to dream
keep doing ~, continue in a state (te-form + いる)

grammar: 消すな is a blunt prohibition (V-dictionary + な). ずっと夢を見てて is a request using the te-form of 見ている with the final いる omitted colloquially — 'please keep on dreaming (so I continue to exist)'.

text: なんだか疲れちゃった
translation: I'm somehow... tired.

vocabulary.meaning: somehow, for some reason, I don't know why but...
to become tired, to grow weary
ended up doing ~ (contraction of てしまった, often with regret or completion)

grammar: 〜ちゃった (< てしまった) expresses that the state of tiredness has fully arrived, often with a nuance of resignation. The fayth is expressing weariness from 1,000 years of dreaming.

text: ねえ、君と君のお父さんなら / 僕たちを眠らせてくれるかな
translation: Hey, if it's you and your father — do you think you could let us sleep?

vocabulary.meaning: to put to sleep, to let sleep (causative of 眠る)
to do something for me/us (receiving a favor)
I wonder..., do you think...? (soft wondering)

grammar: 眠らせてくれるかな combines causative (眠らせる) + てくれる (favor done for the speaker) + かな (wondering/hopeful question). The fayth is gently asking Tidus to free the dreaming fayth from their endless vigil.

text: 君とお父さんはシンに触れた / スピラを巡る死の螺旋 / その中心にいるシンにね
translation: You and your father have touched Sin — the Sin at the center of the spiral of death that surrounds Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: to touch, to come into contact with
to go around, to surround, to cycle through

grammar: The sentence ends with ね, adding a soft explanatory or confirmatory tone. その中心にいるシンにね is a postposed clarification — 'the Sin who is at its center, you see' — a common spoken Japanese pattern where extra detail is added after the main clause.

text: わけわかんねえよ
translation: This makes no sense!
grammar: わけわかんねえ is colloquial contraction of わけがわからない ('the meaning/reason is not understood'). わかんねえ = わからない in casual male speech. Tidus venting frustration at the fayth's cryptic explanation.

text: 君たちはもうただの夢じゃない
translation: You two are no longer just dreams.
grammar: もう〜じゃない means 'no longer ~'. ただ + の + noun means 'a mere/simple noun'. The fayth is telling Tidus that he and Jecht have transcended the status of mere dream-constructs.

text: お願い目を開けて
translation: Please, open your eyes.

vocabulary.meaning: te-form used as a request (please do ~)

grammar: The te-form 開けて functions as a soft imperative request. Combined with お願い at the start, the overall tone is a heartfelt plea rather than a command.

text: もう少し走ってみせてよ
translation: Run a little more — show us you can.

vocabulary.meaning: a little more, a bit more
to do ~ and show (demonstrate), to prove that one can do ~
sentence-final particle adding urgency or emphasis

grammar: 〜てみせる literally means 'do and show/demonstrate'. Here the fayth is asking Tidus to keep going — to prove his existence through action. The pattern conveys demonstration or proving something.

text: 君は、夢を終わらせる夢に、なれるかもしれない。
translation: You might be able to become the dream that ends the dream.

vocabulary.meaning: to bring to an end, to finish (causative of 終わる)
to be able to become (potential form of なる)
might be, there is a possibility that

grammar: 夢を終わらせる夢 is a noun phrase using a relative clause: 'the dream [that] ends [the] dream'. なれるかもしれない = potential form (なれる) + かもしれない, expressing possibility. This is the fayth's central prophecy about Tidus's role.

text: 大丈夫?
translation: Are you okay?
grammar: A bare noun used as a yes/no question by rising intonation. One of the most common expressions in Japanese, functioning both as 'are you okay?' and 'it's okay'.

text: よかった。もう、すんごく心配したんだから!
translation: Thank goodness. I was so, so worried about you!

vocabulary.meaning: I'm glad, thank goodness, what a relief
extremely, incredibly (colloquial intensifier, from すごく)

grammar: 〜んだから is an explanatory pattern adding emotional weight — 'because I was worried, you see!' すんごく is a casual intensification of すごく. Rikku's relief is expressed with characteristic energy.

text: 大丈夫?
translation: Are you okay?
grammar: Same expression repeated by another party member checking on Tidus after his encounter with the fayth.

text: うん。 / どうしたの? / なんでもないよ
translation: Yeah. / What happened? / It's nothing.
grammar: どうしたの is a very common expression using the past tense of どうする + the の question particle: literally 'what did [you/it] do?' but meaning 'what happened?' or 'what's the matter?'. なんでもないよ — the よ adds gentle assertion.

text: 気を失って夢見てた
translation: I passed out and had a dream.

vocabulary.meaning: to lose consciousness, to pass out
was doing ~ (contraction of ていた, past progressive)

grammar: 気を失って (te-form) connects two sequential actions: first he lost consciousness, then he was dreaming. 夢見てた is a contraction of 夢を見ていた — casual spoken Japanese often drops the い of ている.

text: みんなに呼ばれて目が覚めた
translation: Everyone called out to me and I woke up.

vocabulary.meaning: to call, to call out to
to be called by ~, to have ~ call out to one
to wake up, to have one's eyes open

grammar: 呼ばれて is the passive te-form of 呼ぶ — 'being called'. 目が覚める is an idiomatic expression meaning 'to wake up'. The two clauses connect causally: being called caused him to wake.

text: よく寝たし気力回復
translation: Got a good sleep, energy fully restored!
grammar: 〜し connects two related clauses ('I slept well, and so...'). 気力回復 is a nominal sentence with the copula omitted — very casual, energetic speech. Rikku's characteristic cheerfulness as she deflects the heavy mood.

text: じゃあ行くっす
translation: Alright, let's go then!

vocabulary.meaning: casual/youthful copula (from です), adds light politeness

grammar: 行くっす is a youthful/casual speech pattern where っす (≈ です compressed) is added to a plain verb form. It sounds energetic and slightly polite without being formal — typical of Rikku's speech register.

text: そろそろ来るはずだ / 召喚師の力を試すために
translation: It should be coming soon — to test the summoner's power.

vocabulary.meaning: should be, is expected to (logical expectation)
in order to ~, for the purpose of ~

grammar: はずだ expresses logical expectation based on known information — Auron knows a trial guardian is coming. 〜ために indicates purpose: 'for the purpose of testing'.

text: 奴は魔物を放った / 誰が…ですか?
translation: He released a monster. / Who… did?

vocabulary.meaning: to release, to set free, to unleash

grammar: 奴 is a blunt, somewhat contemptuous pronoun for a male person. 放った is the plain past tense of 放つ. 誰が…ですか is an incomplete question — the speaker trails off in surprise, leaving the sentence unfinished.

text: ザナルカンドで強い召喚士を待っている
translation: He is waiting in Zanarkand for a powerful summoner.

vocabulary.meaning: is doing ~, is in the state of ~ (progressive/ongoing)

grammar: 〜ている here expresses an ongoing state (waiting) rather than a momentary action. Auron reveals that someone in Zanarkand has been awaiting a strong summoner.

text: 生きていらっしゃる / マイカやシーモアと同じだ
translation: He is still alive — the same as Maika and Seymour.

vocabulary.meaning: to be (honorific form of いる)

grammar: いらっしゃる is the honorific form of いる, showing respect. Combined with 生きて (te-form of 生きる), 生きていらっしゃる means 'is alive' in formal/respectful language. The comparison to Maika and Seymour — unsent dead who refuse to pass on — is ominous.

text: おじけづいたか? / いいえ
translation: Are you frightened? / No.

vocabulary.meaning: to become frightened, to lose one's nerve, to flinch

grammar: おじけづいたか is a direct past tense question using the plain form — appropriate for Auron's terse, warrior-like speech. Yuna's いいえ is simply the formal 'no', calm and resolute.

text: もう何も怖くないんです / フン、ブラスカの娘だな
translation: I'm no longer afraid of anything. / Hmph. Braska's daughter, indeed.

vocabulary.meaning: nothing ~ (total negation with a negative verb)

grammar: もう何も怖くない uses double negation for emphasis: もう (no longer) + 何も (nothing) + くない (not scary). 〜んです adds a personal/explanatory nuance. Auron's フン, ブラスカの娘だな is a gruff compliment — だな seeks mild agreement/confirms his impression.

text: 最後までそうありたいと思っています
translation: I hope to remain that way until the very end.

vocabulary.meaning: until the very end, to the last
to think that ~, to feel that ~

grammar: そうありたいと思っています: そうある = 'to be that way', ありたい = 'want to be', と思っています = 'I think/feel'. The continuous ています shows an ongoing mental state. Yuna's resolve is expressed with quiet dignity.

text: ねぇ、ちょっと休憩しない? / 休む必要はない。あと一息で山頂だ
translation: Hey, don't you want to take a little break? / There's no need to rest. We're just one push away from the summit.

vocabulary.meaning: don't you want to ~? (negative question as invitation)
just one more effort, just a little more

grammar: 〜ない? as a negative question is a common way to make a soft invitation ('won't you?'). あと一息 is an idiom meaning 'just one more breath of effort'. Auron's terse reply contrasts with Rikku's casual request.

text: あとちょっとだから休みたいんだってば!
translation: That's exactly why I want to rest — because we're almost there!

vocabulary.meaning: just a little more, almost there
I'm telling you! (emphatic repetition expressing frustration)

grammar: 〜んだってば is a strong emphatic ending combining んだ (explanation) + ってば (insistence, 'I said!', 'I keep telling you'). Rikku is exasperated that Auron won't listen, and her logic is charmingly backwards — she wants a rest precisely because the end is near.

text: 考える時間、少ししかないんだもん
translation: There's so little time left to think things over.

vocabulary.meaning: there is only a little (negative + しか = only)

grammar: 〜しかない means 'only (small amount)' — しか requires a negative verb form. 〜んだもん is a childlike or soft-plaintive explanatory ending, warmer/more emotional than 〜んだから. Rikku is revealing her true anxiety under the cheerful surface.

text: ユック… / いいよ、歩きながら考えるから
translation: Rikku... / It's okay, I'll think as I walk.

vocabulary.meaning: it's okay, it's fine, don't worry
while doing ~, at the same time as ~

grammar: 〜ながら expresses simultaneous action ('while walking'). The から at the end is a soft explanatory closer — 'because I will'. Yuna is gently reassuring Rikku while showing her own resolve.

text: 落とした。行こうぜ。
translation: Let it go. Come on, let's move.

vocabulary.meaning: to drop; here figuratively: to let it drop, to leave it

grammar: 落とした here is used figuratively — 'drop it/I've let it go' — Tidus signaling the subject is closed. 行こうぜ is the volitional (let's ~) form of 行く + ぜ, a masculine particle adding energy or urgency.

text: 本当に、もうすぐなんだよな。
translation: It's really almost time, isn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: it is, you know... (explanatory + seeking confirmation, reflective)

grammar: 〜なんだよな combines the explanatory んだ, the assertive よ, and the seeking-confirmation な — together this creates a reflective, musing tone: 'it really is almost time, huh'. Tidus is quietly processing what's coming.

text: とうとうここまで来ちまったな。
translation: We've finally come this far, haven't we.

vocabulary.meaning: finally, at last (after a long time)
ended up doing ~, went and did ~ (colloquial てしまった)

grammar: とうとう emphasizes that the endpoint was a long time coming. 来ちまった is colloquial for 来てしまった — the しまった component can express completion with a mixture of inevitability and sometimes emotional weight.

text: 何がおかしいんだよ。 / 昔の俺と同じだ。
translation: What's so funny? / You're just like I was back then.
grammar: 何がおかしいんだよ: 何が (what subject) + おかしい (funny/wrong) + んだよ (emphatic). Auron responds with 昔の俺と同じだ — a simple nominal predicate sentence meaning 'it's the same as I was in the past', implying he recognizes the tension Tidus is feeling.

text: あの時、ザナルカンドに近づくほど、俺も揺れた。
translation: Back then, the closer we got to Zanarkand, the more I too was shaken.

vocabulary.meaning: the more ~, to the extent that ~
to sway, to waver, to be shaken (emotionally)

grammar: 近づくほど uses ほど in its proportional sense: 'the more [one] approaches, the more...'. 揺れた is used figuratively for emotional wavering. Auron is opening up about his inner state during Braska's pilgrimage a decade ago.

text: たどり着いたらブラスカは究極召喚を得て / シンと戦い、死ぬ
translation: Once we got there, Braska would obtain the Final Summoning — and fight Sin, and die.

vocabulary.meaning: to finally reach, to arrive at after great effort

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

grammar: 〜たら is a conditional form expressing 'once/when ~ happens'. The plain non-past 死ぬ at the end is stark — Auron recounts the known, inevitable outcome with brutal directness.

text: 旅の始めから覚悟していたはずだったが / いざその時が迫ると、怖くなってな
translation: I should have been prepared from the start of the journey — but when the moment actually drew near, I became afraid.

vocabulary.meaning: to prepare oneself, to steel oneself, to accept what is coming
was supposed to be, should have been (unfulfilled expectation)
now that it comes to it, when the moment arrives
to draw near, to press close, to be imminent

grammar: はずだった expresses a past expectation that didn't hold: 'I was supposed to have been prepared'. いざ～と is a pattern meaning 'when it actually comes to ~'. Auron admits genuine fear — a rare moment of vulnerability from him.

text: なんつーか、意外です / 伝説のガードでも迷ったりするなんて
translation: It's kind of... unexpected. That even a legendary guardian would waver like that.

vocabulary.meaning: how do I put it, kind of... (colloquial 何というか)
to hesitate, to waver, to lose one's way
the fact that ~, can you believe that ~ (expressing surprise)

grammar: なんつーか is a colloquial filler from 何というか. 〜たりするなんて: 〜たり adds a 'things like' or 'even ~ and such' nuance, while なんて expresses surprise. Wakka is expressing genuine surprise at Auron's admission.

text: 何が伝説なものか
translation: What's legendary about it?

vocabulary.meaning: as if ~!, don't be ridiculous (strong rhetorical denial)

grammar: 〜なものか is a rhetorical pattern strongly rejecting the preceding claim: 'as if there's anything legendary about it!' It expresses self-deprecation or dismissal. Auron deflects the 'legendary guardian' title.

text: あの頃の俺はただの若造だ / ちょうどお前ぐらいの歳だったな / 何かを変えたいと願ってはいたが 結局は何もできなかった
translation: I was just a young fool back then — about the same age as you. I wanted to change something, but in the end I couldn't do anything.

vocabulary.meaning: to wish, to hope, to desire
in the end, after all, ultimately

grammar: ただの若造だ uses ただ ('merely') + の + noun. 〜てはいたが is a concessive pattern: 'although I was doing ~, ...'. 結局 marks the decisive negative outcome. Auron's rare moment of full honesty about his past failures.

text: それが俺の物語だ
translation: That is my story.
grammar: A simple, declarative sentence — X が Y だ. The word 物語 echoes Tidus's earlier use of the same word ('this is my story'), now applied to Auron. It closes his rare moment of vulnerability with quiet finality.

text: 1,000年前に滅んだ年
translation: The city that was destroyed a thousand years ago.

vocabulary.meaning: to be destroyed, to perish, to fall
town, city (note: written as 年 but read まち in this context — likely 街)

grammar: 1,000年前に滅んだ is a relative clause modifying 年(まち)/街 — 'the city that perished 1,000 years ago'. に marks the point in time. Tidus's narration as the party surveys Zanarkand in the distance.

text: この目で確かめたいと思っていた街
translation: The city I had wanted to see with my own eyes.

vocabulary.meaning: with my own eyes (emphasis on personal witnessing)
to confirm, to check, to verify, to see for oneself

grammar: この目で is an idiomatic expression meaning 'with these very eyes'. 〜たいと思っていた is a layered form: たい (want to) + と思う (think/feel) + ていた (was doing/was in that state) — expressing a long-held desire now finally being fulfilled.

text: リューナの旅の目的地
translation: The destination of Yuna's journey.
grammar: A noun phrase used in narration, with の as the possessive linking 'Yuna's journey' to 'destination'. The ellipsis (implied だ/である) is common in inner monologue and literary narration.

text: 俺の物語の最終章なのか
translation: Is this the final chapter of my story?

vocabulary.meaning: is it ~? (questioning one's own thoughts, rhetorical/internal)

grammar: 〜なのか uses the explanatory の + か to pose a reflective internal question — Tidus is not really asking someone else but questioning himself. The の softens the question and adds an introspective quality.

text: 色んな想いが… / 浮かんでは消えていった / 言葉にならずに…
translation: All sorts of feelings... / rose up and then faded away / without becoming words...

vocabulary.meaning: various, all sorts of (colloquial 色々な)
to float up, to rise, to come to mind
does ~ and then ~ (repeated alternation: rose and faded, rose and faded)
to fade away, to disappear into the distance
to become words, to be put into words

grammar: 浮かんでは消えていった uses the 〜ては〜 pattern to describe repeated alternation ('kept rising and fading'). 言葉にならずに: ならず is the negative te-form of なる, meaning 'without becoming words'. Ellipses (...) capture the wordless quality of the moment.

text: 通り過ぎていった
translation: They just passed on by.

vocabulary.meaning: to pass by, to pass through, to go past
went along doing ~, passed doing ~ (directional movement away from speaker)

grammar: 〜ていった (te-form + 行った) expresses movement away — the feelings are not just gone but have passed onward. The continuation from the previous segment creates a melancholic poetic rhythm in Tidus's narration.

text: みんな、本当にいいの? / あそこに着いたら、優難は…
translation: Everyone — is this really okay? / Once we get there, Yuna will...

vocabulary.meaning: is it okay? are you sure? (soft question with の)

grammar: いいの? uses the の question particle for a softer, emotionally loaded question — Rikku is not demanding an answer but expressing her anxiety. The sentence あそこに着いたら、優難は… is left deliberately unfinished — the ellipsis carrying the unsaid word 'die'.

text: リュックの気持ちはとてもうれしいんだ
translation: I'm so happy for Rikku's feelings — the way she cares.
grammar: リュックの気持ちはとてもうれしいんだ: 気持ち here refers to Rikku's feelings/concern, used as the subject. Yuna is saying she is moved/glad by Rikku's concern for her. 〜んだ adds personal emotional weight to the statement.

text: でもね
translation: But...
grammar: でもね is a gentle adversative — 'but, you know'. The ね softens the turn, giving Yuna's 'but' a tender rather than harsh quality. She pauses before continuing her resolution.

text: もう引き返さない
translation: I won't turn back anymore.

vocabulary.meaning: to turn back, to go back, to retrace one's steps

grammar: もう〜ない: もう with a negative verb means 'no longer' or 'not anymore'. Yuna's declaration is final and calm — she has made her peace with her fate.

text: 引き返せなんて言わないよ
translation: I'm not saying you should turn back.

vocabulary.meaning: things like ~, the idea that ~ (often dismissive)

grammar: 引き返せ is the imperative of 引き返す. 〜なんて here marks the quoted command dismissively: 'I'm not saying (anything like) turn back'. Rikku clarifies she's not asking Yuna to abandon the journey.

text: でも考えようよ / ユーナ助かる方法考えようよ
translation: But let's think — let's think of a way to save Yuna!

vocabulary.meaning: to be saved, to survive, to escape danger

grammar: 考えようよ is the volitional form (〜よう) + よ for encouragement: 'let's think!'. ユーナ助かる方法 is a noun phrase with a relative clause: 'a method by which Yuna is saved'. Rikku is desperately pushing for an alternative.

text: 考えたら / 迷うかもしれないから
translation: If I think about it / I might start to waver.

vocabulary.meaning: to hesitate, to waver, to be lost

grammar: Yuna's devastating honesty: 考えたら (conditional 'if I think') + 迷うかもしれないから (because I might waver). She is not avoiding thought out of ignorance — she is deliberately choosing not to think because she knows it could break her resolve.

text: ユーナ
translation: Yuna...
grammar: A single name spoken with no predicate — expressing emotional impact through silence. Rikku (or Tidus) is speechless after Yuna's admission.

text: ありがとう / リュック
translation: Thank you / Rikku.
grammar: ありがとう with the name added after is warm and personal. The split across two short phrases — gratitude followed by the name — gives it an emotional weight beyond a simple thanks.

text: 大好きだよ
translation: I love you.

vocabulary.meaning: to love greatly, to be very fond of
it is (copula + よ for warm assertion)

grammar: 大好きだよ is one of the most direct and warm expressions of love/affection in Japanese. Unlike 愛してる (romantic love), 大好き can express deep friendship or family love — here from Yuna to Rikku, her cousin. The よ adds personal warmth.

text: 嫌だよユーナ
translation: No, Yuna — I don't want this.

vocabulary.meaning: I don't want, no, I hate this
sentence-final particle for emphasis or appeal

grammar: 嫌だよ expresses strong emotional refusal or distress — 'I don't want this!'. Rikku is crying out against Yuna's impending fate, not literally refusing to go but expressing grief.

text: そんなこと言っちゃ嫌だよ
translation: Don't say things like that.

vocabulary.meaning: I hate it when you ~, don't ~ (prohibition through emotional appeal)

grammar: 〜ちゃ (contraction of ては) followed by 嫌だ creates an emotional prohibition: 'if you say that, I hate it' = 'please don't say that'. Rikku is crying and pleading.

text: シドさんによろしく
translation: Give my regards to Cid.

vocabulary.meaning: regards, please take care of, please give my best

grammar: シドさんによろしく is a set farewell expression: 'please pass along (my regards) to Cid'. The verb (伝えてください) is entirely omitted — common in polite, set phrases. Yuna saying this to Rikku is a quiet, heartbreaking goodbye.

text: 嫌だよ!自分で言いなよ!
translation: No! Say it yourself!
grammar: 言いなよ is 言いな (casual imperative of 言う) + よ. The casual imperative here expresses emotional outburst — Rikku is refusing to accept this as a farewell, insisting Yuna will survive to tell her father herself.

text: お願い… / そんなこと言わないでよ!
translation: Please... / Don't say things like that!

vocabulary.meaning: please don't say (negative te-form as request)

grammar: 言わないでよ: 言わない (negative form of 言う) + で (te-form as request) + よ (for emotional appeal). Together: 'please don't say (such things)!' — Rikku's cry of grief.

text: もう会えなくなるみたいで嫌だよ!
translation: It's like we'll never be able to meet again — I hate it!

vocabulary.meaning: to become unable to ~ (potential negative + なる)
it's like ~, it seems like ~ (te-form as cause/reason)
I hate this, I don't want this

grammar: 会えなくなる: 会える (can meet, potential) + なく (negative conjunctive) + なる (become) = 'will become unable to meet'. みたいで: みたい is a comparison/likeness suffix, and the te-form here shows it as the reason for 嫌だ. 'It feels like we'll never meet again and I hate that'.

text: キマリー…行こう!
translation: Kimahri... let's go!

vocabulary.meaning: let's go (volitional form of 行く)

grammar: Yuna calls Kimahri's name and uses the volitional 行こう to move the group forward — gently pulling away from Rikku's grief to continue the journey. The name followed by ellipsis and then action captures the emotional weight of the moment.

text: アーロンさん / キマリから聞きました。私をベベルから連れ出せという父さんの言葉。
translation: Auron. / I heard from Kimahri — my father's words telling you to take me out of Bevelle.

vocabulary.meaning: to hear, to listen, to learn
to take out, to lead out, to bring out
the ~ that says, called ~ (quoting or describing)

grammar: 私をベベルから連れ出せという父さんの言葉: 連れ出せ is the imperative of 連れ出す, embedded in a quote with という, modifying 言葉. The full structure is: 'father's words [which said] take Yuna out of Bevelle'. Yuna has pieced together the truth about Auron's mission.

text: キマリに伝えたのは、アーロンさんですよね。
translation: It was you who passed that message to Kimahri, wasn't it, Auron.

vocabulary.meaning: to convey, to pass along, to transmit
it is ~ who ~ (nominalized cleft sentence for emphasis)
isn't it, right? (seeking confirmation with gentle certainty)

grammar: キマリに伝えたのは uses nominalization (〜の) to create a cleft structure: 'the one who conveyed to Kimahri was...'. ですよね combines polite です, assertion よ, and confirmation-seeking ね — Yuna is not really asking but confirming what she knows.

text: いつかお会いしたいと思っていました。
translation: I had always hoped to meet you someday.

vocabulary.meaning: to meet (humble/polite form of 会う)
had been wanting to ~, had hoped to ~

grammar: お会いする is the humble form of 会う, showing respect toward Auron. 〜たいと思っていました: たい (desire) + と思う (think) + ていました (was in that state, past continuous) — 'I had been thinking/hoping that I wanted to meet you'. Yuna's quiet acknowledgment of her father's legacy and Auron's role in it.
